To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the magnetization plateaus of the antiferromagetic spin-1 Ising chain with random exchange constants and a crystal-field interaction, can be related to the ground state of the system, when the field is changed; (b) the plateaus are present only when the Bernoulli random exchange constant distribution is considered; (c) the plateaus disappear as the Gaussian random exchange distribution is considered.

The presence and the nature of magnetization plateaus in a disordered Ising chain with crystal field and random exchange constants depends on the type of disorder and the strength of the crystal field.

(1) for Bernoulli disorder, the number of magnetization plateaus increases with the width of the distribution; (2) the magnetization plateaus appear at the same magnetic fields as those of the uniform case; (3) for Gaussian distributions, the number of magnetic plateaus decreases as the disorder increases, and (4) the magnetization plateau structure disappears for large disorder widths.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effect of quenched disorder on the presence of magnetization plateaus in a spin-1 Ising chain with crystal field.
the study of the magnetization of a spin chain in the presence of a random distribution of exchange constants and a crystal field.
the study of the magnetization of an Ising chain with random quenched disorder, in the presence of an external uniform magnetic filed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of plateaux in the magnetization of the model is a robust feature, which does not disappear even when the exchange constants are quenched random variables.
the presence of quenched disorder does not destroy the plateaus, but it can modify their structure.
the plateaus are present for the Gaussian distribution only for very narrow widths, but the number of plateaux increases with the width of the Bernoulli distributions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the presence of disorder, the magnetization plateaus are not destroyed, but they are shifted in the field axis.
the presence of plateaux in the magnetization of an anisotropic Ising antiferromagnet with quenched disorder is strongly dependent on the nature of the distribution of exchange interactions.
the presence of disorder, for the Bernoulli case, can lead to a more complicated magnetization behavior, with respect to a uniform system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of a random distribution of exchange constants, there is a strong correlation between the ground-state structure and the plateaus observed on the magnetization curves.
the number of plateaux increases with the width of the distribution, and the number of plateaues increases with the width.

the presence of plateaux in the magnetization curve can be linked to a ground-state phase transition, which occurs as the magnetic field is changed, and the crystal-field anisotropy plays a crucial role.
